entities.label: Native α345(IV)NC1 hexamer
entities.description: Cross-linked type IV collagen NC1 assembly; native and dissociated conformations differ in antibody accessibility in the cited biochemical assays.

entities.label: Exposed α3/α5 NC1 epitopes
entities.description: Conformational Goodpasture antibody epitopes on dissociated α3NC1 and α5NC1; distinct from the linear T-cell peptide.

entities.label: Anti-GBM IgG
entities.description: Patient autoantibodies recognizing collagen IV NC1 domains; distinct from heterologous experimental antiserum.

entities.label: GBM-bound IgG
entities.description: Antibody bound along glomerular basement membrane, commonly seen as linear IgG staining.

entities.label: HLA-DR15 presentation
entities.description: Presentation of α3 135–145 T-cell peptide by HLA-DR15; genotype does not determine disease in every carrier.

entities.label: α3-specific CD4 T cells
entities.description: Autoreactive CD4 T cells recognizing α3 135–145; human expansion and mouse induction findings are distinguished.

entities.label: HLA-DR1-selected regulatory T cells
entities.description: α3-specific regulatory T cells in HLA-DR1/DR15 transgenic experiments and healthy human donor phenotyping.

entities.label: Complement activation / deposits
entities.description: Classical and alternative complement involvement assessed using human tissue staining and separate heterologous-antibody mouse experiments.

entities.label: Neutrophils
entities.description: Innate effector cells; perturbational evidence here comes from heterologous anti-GBM animal models.

entities.label: Renal inflammation / injury
entities.description: Study-specific glomerulonephritis, proteinuria or renal function outcomes; animal and human observations remain separate.

entities.label: Glomerular crescent formation
entities.description: Crescentic glomerular pathology; association with complement staining does not establish its causal initiation.

entities.label: Alveolar haemorrhage / lung injury
entities.description: Human pulmonary manifestation and experimental rat haemorrhagic lung injury; not present in all patients.

entities.label: Imlifidase
entities.description: IgG-cleaving enzyme investigated for severe anti-GBM disease; antibody removal and clinical efficacy are separate outcomes.

entities.label: Plasma exchange + immunosuppression
entities.description: Combined plasma exchange, cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoids; observational outcomes cannot isolate individual component effects.

entities.label: ANCA/anti-GBM double positivity
entities.description: Labelled overlap with ANCA-associated vasculitis; not an inferred universal progression from one disease to another.

claims.text: In biochemical assays, the native cross-linked α345NC1 hexamer concealed antibody-reactive conformations present on α3NC1/α5NC1 monomers.
limitations: Does not establish the initiating in-vivo trigger or prove that hexamer disruption precedes human disease.

claims.text: Patient kidney/lung-bound autoantibodies recognized α3NC1 and α5NC1 monomers in antigen-specificity assays.
limitations: Binding specificity does not show equal pathogenic contribution of α3 and α5 antibodies; Alport comparators are excluded as mapped disease.

claims.text: Anti-GBM antibodies were identified in sera/kidneys and bound host glomeruli in the reported human cases.
limitations: Historical selected cases; modern prevalence, diagnosis and transplantation inferences from this report are not adopted.

claims.text: Transfer of serum or renal-eluate IgG from three anti-GBM patients produced acute glomerulonephritis in recipient monkeys.
limitations: Passive transfer supports antibody pathogenicity in recipients; it does not explain human autoimmunity initiation.

claims.text: In HLA-DR15 transgenic mice, α3 peptide presentation selected pro-inflammatory conventional α3-specific T-cell responses.
limitations: Abstract-level mouse mechanism; not all human HLA-DR15 carriers develop anti-GBM disease.

claims.text: Patients with Goodpasture disease displayed clonally expanded α3-specific CD4 T-cell repertoires.
limitations: Expansion in patients does not establish that T cells alone caused their renal injury.

claims.text: After α3 peptide immunization, α3-specific T cells infiltrated kidneys and HLA-DR15 transgenic mice developed disease.
limitations: Induced disease model; antibody-independent injury is not established by this abstract passage.

claims.text: HLA-DR1-induced regulatory T cells conferred resistance to induced disease in HLA-DR15/DR1 transgenic mice.
limitations: Protective model branch; this does not demonstrate clinical Treg therapy efficacy.

claims.text: Anti-GBM renal biopsies showed complement components along GBM, including classical and alternative-pathway components.
limitations: Tissue colocalization does not establish pathway ordering or complement dependence in each patient; two patients were MPO-ANCA positive.

claims.text: Factor B and C5b-9 staining was stronger in glomeruli with crescents than in glomeruli without crescents.
limitations: Small observational biopsy study with glomeruli nested within patients; not proof of complement-caused crescents.

claims.text: C3- or C4-deficient mice had reduced early glomerular neutrophil infiltration after heterologous anti-GBM antibody challenge.
limitations: Heterologous acute model; not direct evidence for complement blockade in human anti-GBM disease.

claims.text: C3 or C4 deficiency reduced proteinuria and capillary thrombosis in heterologous anti-GBM nephritis.
limitations: Dose-sensitive model effect; protection was overcome by increased antibody dose.

claims.text: Increasing nephritogenic antibody dose overcame the protective effect of complement deficiency.
limitations: Qualifies absolute complement dependence; cannot be used as positive evidence that complement is always necessary.

claims.text: Neutrophils were required for full haemorrhagic lung injury after anti-GBM antibody infusion in rats.
limitations: Rat lung injury model; does not establish sufficiency of the same pathway in human alveolar haemorrhage.

claims.text: Complement was required for full anti-GBM antibody-induced haemorrhagic lung injury in rats.
limitations: Same study as neutrophil lung result, not independent replication; acute model.

claims.text: Double-positive patients shared severe renal disease and frequent lung haemorrhage at presentation with anti-GBM disease.
limitations: Overlap link to ANCA-associated vasculitis only; not evidence that ANCA causes anti-GBM antibodies.

claims.text: In the 15-adult one-arm phase 2a trial, anti-GBM antibody levels were below the assay reference range six hours after imlifidase.
limitations: Uncontrolled phase 2a study; antibody depletion is a pharmacodynamic endpoint, not proof of added clinical benefit; six patients also ANCA positive.

claims.text: Ten of fifteen phase 2a participants were dialysis independent at six months, compared with nine of fifty historical controls.
limitations: Historical comparison subject to selection and care differences; later randomized phase 3 sponsor report found no significant primary-endpoint benefit.

claims.text: In 71 patients treated with plasma exchange, prednisolone and cyclophosphamide, renal outcomes varied greatly with baseline renal severity.
limitations: No untreated randomized comparator; cannot estimate independent efficacy of plasma exchange, cyclophosphamide or glucocorticoids.

claims.text: All patients requiring immediate dialysis with 100% crescents remained dialysis dependent in the treated cohort.
limitations: Selected cohort prognosis; not a universal futility rule, especially for pulmonary haemorrhage.

scientificSummary.scope: Bounded anti-GBM autoimmunity to alpha3/alpha5 type IV collagen NC1 epitopes, HLA-restricted T-cell responses, antibody-mediated renal and pulmonary injury; human observations and experimental models remain distinct. Excludes Alport post-transplant nephritis and atypical seronegative disease.

paragraphs.text: Classical anti-GBM disease links autoimmunity against type IV collagen NC1 domains with antibody deposition and glomerular injury, sometimes accompanied by pulmonary haemorrhage. Patient antibodies recognize α3NC1 and α5NC1 conformations that are concealed in the native cross-linked α345NC1 hexamer in biochemical assays; the initiating disruption in patients remains unresolved. Human α3-specific CD4 T-cell expansion supports an autoimmune response, while peptide-immunized HLA-DR15 transgenic mice demonstrate nephritogenic T-cell responses and HLA-DR1-associated regulatory protection. Patient IgG transfer caused glomerulonephritis in monkeys. Human biopsies associate complement deposition with crescentic injury; separate heterologous-antibody models support complement-dependent neutrophil recruitment and renal injury in mice and complement/neutrophil contributions to haemorrhagic lung injury in rats. These findings form a contextual synthesis, rather than proof that every step occurs in one human causal sequence.

Important limits remain: complement-deficient mice lost protection at higher antibody doses, and human staining does not establish universal pathway dependence. The labelled ANCA/anti-GBM overlap has its own clinical context. Combined plasma exchange, cyclophosphamide and glucocorticoids is guideline-recommended treatment with defined exceptions; the selected historical cohort shows strong dependence of renal recovery on baseline severity and cannot isolate component effects. Imlifidase rapidly depleted circulating anti-GBM antibodies in a 15-adult uncontrolled phase 2a study, whose historical-control comparison suggested renal benefit. However, the sponsor subsequently reported that the 50-patient randomized GOOD-IDES-02 trial missed its six-month eGFR primary endpoint with similar responses in both arms. Antibody removal therefore cannot be equated with added clinical benefit. Imlifidase remains investigational for this mapped indication; its EU transplant indication is separate. This bounded draft relies predominantly on selected abstracts, omits newer antigen and targeted-cell-therapy branches, and requires independent scientific review.
